prerequisites: Submission of tasks from exercises in appropriate quality.
syllabus_topics: Nature and mechanisms of corrosion; corrosion in non-conductive media
Corrosion in oxidizing and reducing atmospheres; heat-resistant materials
Corrosion in electrically conductive media; polarization curves; types of corrosion attack
Atmospheric corrosion; atmospheric corrosion-resistant steels
Passivation and classification of corrosion-resistant steels based on equilibrium diagrams
Chromium martensitic and super-martensitic steels; ferritic and super-ferritic steels
Austenitic and super-austenitic steels; duplex stainless steels; martensitic-austenitic steels and SAF grades
Nickel, cobalt, and titanium alloys and their applications; non-metallic corrosion-resistant materials
Corrosion resistance testing
Nature and mechanisms of creep strength and relaxation; characteristics of creep-resistant materials; creep limit, creep rupture strength, relaxation limit
Boiler materials for conventional power plants
Boiler materials for supercritical power plants
Steam turbine blade and rotor materials; steels for turbogenerator components
Steels for selected nuclear power plant components; pressure vessel and primary piping
Nickel-based creep-resistant materials
Nickel oxidation kinetics
Corrosion characteristics from polarization curves
Atmospheric corrosion kinetics and service life determination
Applicability of the Schaeffler diagram
Methods for evaluating creep curves
Service life based on the Larson-Miller parameter
Final test
bibliography: [1] BRUMOVSKY, M. Materials used for the design and contruction of WWER comonents, INR 2006
